doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First organ on the road with John Patton, and Grant Green
summary: Patton was his first road organist; he never took the addicted Grant Green on the road.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: When you started carrying an organ, it’s about 1960...
The first organist you traveled with extensively was John Patton, although you’d been doing some gigs with Jimmy Smith before that.
Yeah, John Patton was the first one I took on the road.

I don’t know how I met John. It was in New York. I met John Patton, Ben Dixon and Grant Green. We had a nice group. Nice group. I met Grant in East St. Louis, Illinois. In fact, I’m the one who brought him to New York.
Can you separate your assessment of his personality from that, or does that define it
Yeah, he had no personality. A junkie got no personality. Junkie works 24 hours a day trying to get money to get a fix. That’s that personality.
But you must have really liked his playing...
You had with him for several years.
But I didn’t take him on the road.
Oh, no. I never took him once on the road. Because they got the ten-year Mann Act. You cross the line with some drugs, goodbye—you’re gone. I never took him with him me. I didn’t take that change.
